questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | GA Question: 1
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Two processes, $P1$ and $P2$, need to access a critical section of code. Consider the following synchronization construct used by the processes:

/*  P1   */
while (true) {
    wants1 = true;
    while (wants2 == true);
    /* Critical Section */
    wants1 = false;
}
/* Remainder section */

/*  P2   */
while (true) {
    wants2 = true;
    while (wants1 == true);
    /* Critical Section */
    wants2=false;
}
/* Remainder section */

Here, wants$1$ and wants$2$ are shared variables, which are initialized to false.

Which one of the following statements is TRUE about the construct?
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
Two processes, $P1$ and $P2$, need to access a critical section of code. Consider the following synchronization construct used by the processes:

/*  P1   */
while (true) {
    wants1 = true;
    while (wants2 == true);
    /* Critical Section */
    wants1 = false;
}
/* Remainder section */

/*  P2   */
while (true) {
    wants2 = true;
    while (wants1 == true);
    /* Critical Section */
    wants2=false;
}
/* Remainder section */

Here, wants$1$ and wants$2$ are shared variables, which are initialized to false.

Which one of the following statements is TRUE about the construct?

  1. It does not ensure mutual exclusion.

  2. It does not ensure bounded waiting.

  3. It requires that processes enter the critical section in strict alteration.

  4. It does not prevent deadlocks, but ensures mutual exclusion.
options: It does not ensure mutual exclusion.
It does not ensure bounded waiting.
It requires that processes enter the critical section in strict alteration.
It does not prevent deadlocks, but ensures mutual exclusion.

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | GA Question: 2
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Information about a collection of students is given by the relation $\text{studInfo(}\underline{\text{studId}},\text{ name, sex)}$. The relation $\text{enroll(}{\text{studId}},{\text{ courseId}})$ gives which student has enrolled for (or taken) what course(s). Assume that every course is taken by at least one male and at least one female student. What does the following relational algebra expression represent?

$\pi _{courceId}\left(\left(\pi_{\text{studId}}\left(\sigma_{sex=“female"}\left(\text{studInfo}\right)\right) \times \pi_{courseId}\left(\text{enroll}\right)\right) -\text{enroll}\right)$

  1. Courses in which all the female students are enrolled.
  2. Courses in which a proper subset of female students are enrolled.
  3. Courses in which only male students are enrolled.

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | GA Question: 7
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Hari(H), Gita(G), Irfan(I) and Saira(S) are siblings (i.e., brothers and sisters). All were born on $1^{\text{st}}$ January. The age difference between any two successive siblings (that is born one after another) is less than three years. Given the following facts:

  1. Hari's age $+$ Gita's age $>$ Irfan's age $+$ Saira's age
  2. The age difference between Gita and Saira is one year. However Gita is not the oldest and Saira is not the youngest.
  3. There are no twins.

In what order they were born (oldest first)?

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | EC Question: 1
questions.subject: Electronic Devices (EDC)
questions.question: The Einstein relation relating carrier diffusion coefficient $D$ and carrier mobility $\mu$ in a semiconductor at thermal equilibrium temperature $T$ is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electronic Devices (EDC)):

Einstein's relation: $\frac{D_n}{\mu_n} = \frac{D_p}{\mu_p} = \frac{k T}{q} = V_t$ (thermal voltage $\approx 26\text{ mV}$ at $300\text{ K}$).

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | EC Question: 3
questions.subject: Analog Circuits
questions.question: A common-emitter BJT amplifier with unbypassed emitter resistor $R_E$ introduces negative feedback that results in:
options: Increased input resistance and stabilized voltage gain
Decreased input resistance and increased voltage gain
Zero output resistance and unstable gain

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Increased input resistance and stabilized voltage gain
structuredOptions.html: Increased input resistance and stabilized voltage gain

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Decreased input resistance and increased voltage gain
structuredOptions.html: Decreased input resistance and increased voltage gain

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Zero output resistance and unstable gain
structuredOptions.html: Zero output resistance and unstable gain

questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Analog Circuits):

An unbypassed $R_E$ provides series-series negative feedback. This raises the input impedance ($R_{\text{in}} \approx r_\pi + (1+\beta)R_E$), stabilizes gain against $h_{fe}$ variations, and widens bandwidth.

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | EC Question: 11
questions.subject: Digital Circuits
questions.question: The minimum number of 2-to-1 multiplexers required to realize an arbitrary 4-to-1 multiplexer without any external logic gates is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Digital Circuits):

A 4-to-1 multiplexer has 2 select lines. Two 2-to-1 MUXes are used in the first stage driven by $S_0$, and one 2-to-1 MUX is used in the second stage driven by $S_1$. Total MUX count $= 2 + 1 = 3$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | EC Question: 18
questions.subject: Control Systems
questions.question: The steady-state error $e_{ss}$ of a Type-1 unity feedback control system to a unit ramp input $r(t) = t \cdot u(t)$ is given by:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Control Systems):

For a Type-1 system with unit ramp input: velocity error constant $K_v = \lim_{s \to 0} s G(s)$, and steady-state error $e_{ss} = \frac{1}{K_v}$.

questions.question: A non-inverting operational amplifier circuit has $R_1 = 5\,\text{k}\Omega$ connected from the inverting pin to ground and feedback resistor $R_f = 45\,\text{k}\Omega$. The closed-loop voltage gain $A_v = 1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1}$ is ________.

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | EC Question: 28
questions.subject: Digital Circuits
questions.question: A mod-16 ripple counter is built using 4 toggle ($T$) flip-flops. If the input clock frequency is $32\text{ kHz}$, the output frequency (in $\text{kHz}$) at the final flip-flop is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Digital Circuits):

A counter with $N = 4$ flip-flops has modulus $2^N = 16$. Each flip-flop divides frequency by 2: $f_{\text{out}} = \frac{f_{\text{in}}}{16} = \frac{32\text{ kHz}}{16} = 2\text{ kHz}$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | EC Question: 36
questions.subject: Communications & Information Theory
questions.question: An AM broadcast signal has a carrier power $P_c = 10\text{ kW}$ and modulation index $\mu = 0.8$. The total transmitted power $P_t = P_c \left(1 + \frac{\mu^2}{2}\right)$ (in $\text{kW}$) is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Communications & Information Theory):

$P_t = 10 \left(1 + \frac{0.8^2}{2}\right) = 10 \left(1 + \frac{0.64}{2}\right) = 10(1 + 0.32) = 13.2\text{ kW}$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | EC Question: 37
questions.subject: Communications & Information Theory
questions.question: According to Shannon's Channel Capacity theorem, the capacity $C$ of an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel with bandwidth $B$ and signal-to-noise ratio $\text{SNR} = S/N$ is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Communications & Information Theory):

Shannon-Hartley theorem states maximum error-free transmission capacity is $C = B \log_2 (1 + \text{SNR})$ bits/second.

questions.title: GATE EC 2017 | EC Question: 51
questions.subject: Electromagnetics & Antennas
questions.question: A uniform plane electromagnetic wave propagates in free space with permittivity $\epsilon_0$ and permeability $\mu_0$. The intrinsic wave impedance $\eta_0 = \sqrt{\mu_0 / \epsilon_0}$ (in Ohms) is closest to ________ (rounded off to nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electromagnetics & Antennas):

$\eta_0 = \sqrt{\frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7}}{8.854 \times 10^{-12}}} \approx 120\pi \approx 376.99 \approx 377\,\Omega$.
